evidence.observation: The checkout-web dependency path includes payment-api, which depends on auth-gateway; AUTH-2026-0318 is the recent auth-gateway change and rotated the issuer and JWKS cache namespace.

At 14:10Z, checkout-web had an 18.7% HTTP 401 rate and 2400 ms p95 with checkout submits rejected after payment auth; payment-api had a 21.2% 401 rate and notes an invalid issuer; auth-gateway had a 28.4% 401 rate and issuer mismatch.

AUTH-2026-0318 deployed at 14:05Z; auth-gateway then logged a JWKS cache miss and rejected token issuer partner-v2 because only partner-v1 was allowed. The log explicitly identifies restoring partner-v2 or reverting AUTH-2026-0318 as rollback candidates.
Payment token validation failed upstream at auth-gateway with issuer_not_allowed for partner-v2, and request req-8812 was rejected as invalid_issuer before the order-db dependency was used.
Checkout submit req-8812 failed with a 401 from payment-api; checkout-web recorded payment-api auth_failed with invalid issuer while static assets recovered normally.

excluded_red_herrings.why_not_primary: The database reported normal 35 ms query latency and zero errors; no failed checkout transaction reached it because requests stopped at the auth gate.

The metric notes the errors were isolated to images, and checkout-web confirmed static assets served normally after retry while checkout remained blocked. CDN is not on the payment authorization dependency path.
This is a downstream symptom of rejected/failed payment authorization, not evidence of an independent checkout-web fault.

recommended_next_steps: Immediately halt or roll back AUTH-2026-0318, or restore partner-v2 in auth-gateway allowed_issuers using the approved change process.
Repair and invalidate/rebuild the JWKS cache under the intended partner-v2 namespace, then confirm token validation succeeds.
Run a controlled checkout payment authorization and verify a successful payment-api response and downstream order creation.
Monitor HTTP 401 rates and p95 latency for auth-gateway, payment-api, and checkout-web until they return to baseline; separately track CDN image errors and orders-db CPU.
